audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar complaint, shared-spirit, quail, and plague text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Taberah fire, food craving, manna description, Moses' leadership collapse, seventy elders, Eldad and Medad, universal-prophecy wish, quail, and Graves of Craving. Strong burnout, mental-health, anti-authoritarian, and anti-victim-blaming safeguards required.

verses.restored: The people became as complainers, evil in ears of YHWH; YHWH heard, and his anger burned, and fire of YHWH burned among them and consumed at edge of camp.

familiar.text: And when the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.

modern.text: Soon the people began to complain about their hardship in the hearing of the LORD, and when He heard them, His anger was kindled, and fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמִתְאֹ֣נְנִ֔ים רַ֖ע בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ וַיִּ֣חַר אַפּ֔וֹ וַתִּבְעַר בָּם֙ אֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אכַל בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: The people cried to Moses; Moses prayed to YHWH, and fire sank down.

familiar.text: And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the LORD, the fire was quenched.

modern.text: And the people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.

original.text: וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֖ם אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּשְׁקַ֖ע הָאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: He called name of that place Taberah/Burning, because fire of YHWH burned among them.

familiar.text: And he called the name of the place Taberah: because the fire of the LORD burnt among them.

modern.text: So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא תַּבְעֵרָ֑ה כִּֽי בָעֲרָ֥ה בָ֖ם אֵ֥שׁ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: The mixed multitude among them craved a craving, and children of Israel also returned and wept, saying, Who will give us flesh to eat?

familiar.text: And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?

modern.text: Meanwhile, the rabble among them had a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites wept and said, “Who will feed us meat?

original.text: וְהָֽאסַפְסֻף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ הִתְאַוּ֖וּ תַּאֲוָ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיִּבְכּ֗וּ גַּ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י יַאֲכִלֵ֖נוּ בָּשָֽׂר

verses.restored: We remember fish we ate in Egypt for nothing, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.

familiar.text: We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:

modern.text: We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.

original.text: זָכַ֨רְנוּ֙ אֶת הַדָּגָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר נֹאכַ֥ל בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם חִנָּ֑ם אֵ֣ת הַקִּשֻּׁאִ֗ים וְאֵת֙ הָֽאֲבַטִּחִ֔ים וְאֶת הֶחָצִ֥יר וְאֶת הַבְּצָלִ֖ים וְאֶת הַשּׁוּמִֽים

verses.restored: But now our soul/life is dried up; there is nothing at all except this manna before our eyes.

familiar.text: But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.

modern.text: But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing to see but this manna!”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֛ה נַפְשֵׁ֥נוּ יְבֵשָׁ֖ה אֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל בִּלְתִּ֖י אֶל הַמָּ֥ן עֵינֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like bdellium.

familiar.text: And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium.

modern.text: Now the manna resembled coriander seed, and its appearance was like that of gum resin.

original.text: וְהַמָּ֕ן כִּזְרַע גַּ֖ד ה֑וּא וְעֵינ֖וֹ כְּעֵ֥ין הַבְּדֹֽלַח

verses.restored: The people went about and gathered it, ground it in mills or beat it in mortar, cooked it in pots, and made cakes from it; its taste was like taste of cakes with oil.

familiar.text: And the people went about, and gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in a mortar, and baked it in pans, and made cakes of it: and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.

modern.text: The people walked around and gathered it, ground it on a handmill or crushed it in a mortar, then boiled it in a cooking pot or shaped it into cakes. It tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.

original.text: שָׁטוּ֩ הָעָ֨ם וְלָֽקְט֜וּ וְטָחֲנ֣וּ בָרֵחַ֗יִם א֤וֹ דָכוּ֙ בַּמְּדֹכָ֔ה וּבִשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּפָּר֔וּר וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ עֻג֑וֹת וְהָיָ֣ה טַעְמ֔וֹ כְּטַ֖עַם לְשַׁ֥ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן

verses.restored: When dew descended upon camp by night, manna descended upon it.

familiar.text: And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell upon it.

modern.text: When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it. The Complaint of Moses

original.text: וּבְרֶ֧דֶת הַטַּ֛ל עַל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה יֵרֵ֥ד הַמָּ֖ן עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Moses heard the people weeping by clans, each at entrance of his tent; anger of YHWH burned greatly, and in eyes of Moses it was evil.

familiar.text: Then Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent: and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly; Moses also was displeased.

modern.text: Then Moses heard the people of family after family weeping at the entrances to their tents, and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly, and Moses was also displeased.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת הָעָ֗ם בֹּכֶה֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו אִ֖ישׁ לְפֶ֣תַח אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּֽחַר אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וּבְעֵינֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה רָֽע

verses.restored: Moses said to YHWH, Why have you done evil to your servant, and why have I not found favor in your eyes, that you put burden of all this people upon me?

familiar.text: And Moses said unto the LORD, Wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant? and wherefore have I not found favour in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me?

modern.text: So Moses asked the LORD, “Why have You brought this trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have laid upon me the burden of all these people?

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל יְהוָ֗ה לָמָ֤ה הֲרֵעֹ֨תָ֙ לְעַבְדֶּ֔ךָ וְלָ֛מָּה לֹא מָצָ֥תִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ לָשׂ֗וּם אֶת מַשָּׂ֛א כָּל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה עָלָֽי

verses.restored: Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, Carry them in your bosom as nursing guardian carries infant, to ground you swore to their fathers?

familiar.text: Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father beareth the sucking child, unto the land which thou swarest unto their fathers?

modern.text: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth, so that You should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant,’ to the land that You swore to give their fathers?

original.text: הֶאָנֹכִ֣י הָרִ֗יתִי אֵ֚ת כָּל הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אִם אָנֹכִ֖י יְלִדְתִּ֑יהוּ כִּֽי תֹאמַ֨ר אֵלַ֜י שָׂאֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקֶ֗ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשָּׂ֤א הָאֹמֵן֙ אֶת הַיֹּנֵ֔ק עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: From where do I have flesh to give all this people? For they weep to me, saying, Give us flesh that we may eat.

familiar.text: Whence should I have flesh to give unto all this people? for they weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.

modern.text: Where can I get meat for all these people? For they keep crying out to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’

original.text: מֵאַ֤יִן לִי֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר לָתֵ֖ת לְכָל הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי יִבְכּ֤וּ עָלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָה לָּ֥נוּ בָשָׂ֖ר וְנֹאכֵֽלָה

verses.restored: I am not able, I alone, to carry all this people, for it is too heavy for me.

familiar.text: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.

modern.text: I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.

original.text: לֹֽא אוּכַ֤ל אָנֹכִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת כָּל הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֥י כָבֵ֖ד מִמֶּֽנִּי

verses.restored: If thus you do to me, kill me, please kill me, if I have found favor in your eyes, and let me not see my wretchedness.

familiar.text: And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.

modern.text: If this is how You are going to treat me, please kill me right now—if I have found favor in Your eyes—and let me not see my own wretchedness.” Seventy Elders Anointed

original.text: וְאִם כָּ֣כָה אַתְּ עֹ֣שֶׂה לִּ֗י הָרְגֵ֤נִי נָא֙ הָרֹ֔ג אִם מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְאַל אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּרָעָתִֽי

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Gather to me seventy men from elders of Israel, whom you know as elders of people and its officers; take them to tent of meeting, and let them stand there with you.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶסְפָה לִּ֞י שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִישׁ֮ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי הֵ֛ם זִקְנֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם וְשֹׁטְרָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶל אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֥וּ שָׁ֖ם עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: I will come down and speak with you there; I will take from spirit that is upon you and put it upon them, and they shall bear burden of people with you, and you shall not bear it alone.

familiar.text: And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.

modern.text: And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them. They will help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself.

original.text: וְיָרַדְתִּ֗י וְדִבַּרְתִּ֣י עִמְּךָ֮ שָׁם֒ וְאָצַלְתִּ֗י מִן הָר֛וּחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּמַשָּׂ֣א הָעָ֔ם וְלֹא תִשָּׂ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: To people you shall say, Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow and you shall eat flesh, for you wept in ears of YHWH, saying, Who will give us flesh to eat? For it was good for us in Egypt. YHWH will give you flesh, and you shall eat.

familiar.text: And say thou unto the people, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh: for ye have wept in the ears of the LORD, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: therefore the LORD will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.

modern.text: And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, because you have cried out in the hearing of the LORD, saying: ‘Who will feed us meat? For we were better off in Egypt!’ Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.

original.text: וְאֶל הָעָ֨ם תֹּאמַ֜ר הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמָחָר֮ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם בָּשָׂר֒ כִּ֡י בְּכִיתֶם֩ בְּאָזְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֤י יַאֲכִלֵ֨נוּ֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּי ט֥וֹב לָ֖נוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְנָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וַאֲכַלְתֶּֽם

verses.restored: Not one day shall you eat, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,

familiar.text: Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days;

modern.text: You will eat it not for one or two days, nor for five or ten or twenty days,

original.text: לֹ֣א י֥וֹם אֶחָ֛ד תֹּאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֣א יוֹמָ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה יָמִ֗ים וְלֹא֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה יָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֖א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים יֽוֹם

verses.restored: but up to a month of days, until it comes out from your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you rejected YHWH who is in your midst and wept before him, saying, Why did we come out from Egypt?

familiar.text: But even a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome unto you: because that ye have despised the LORD which is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt?

modern.text: but for a whole month—until it comes out of your nostrils and makes you nauseous—because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried out before Him, saying, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’”

original.text: עַ֣ד חֹ֣דֶשׁ יָמִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא֙ מֵֽאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְזָרָ֑א יַ֗עַן כִּֽי מְאַסְתֶּ֤ם אֶת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֔ם וַתִּבְכּ֤וּ לְפָנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה יָצָ֥אנוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Moses said, Six hundred thousand on foot are people in whose midst I am, and you have said, Flesh I will give them, and they shall eat a month of days.

familiar.text: And Moses said, The people, among whom I am, are six hundred thousand footmen; and thou hast said, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a whole month.

modern.text: But Moses replied, “Here I am among 600,000 men on foot, yet You say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a month.’

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ שֵׁשׁ מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֨לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֗רְתָּ בָּשָׂר֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם וְאָכְל֖וּ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים

verses.restored: Shall flock and herd be slaughtered for them and be enough for them? Shall all fish of sea be gathered for them and be enough for them?

familiar.text: Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, to suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?

modern.text: If all our flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? Or if all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?”

original.text: הֲצֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר יִשָּׁחֵ֥ט לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֣א לָהֶ֑ם אִ֣ם אֶֽת כָּל דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֛ם יֵאָסֵ֥ף לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֥א לָהֶֽם

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Is hand of YHWH shortened? Now you shall see whether my word happens to you or not.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Is the LORD’s hand waxed short? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not.

modern.text: The LORD answered Moses, “Is the LORD’s arm too short? Now you will see whether or not My word will come to pass.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה הֲיַ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה תִּקְצָ֑ר עַתָּ֥ה תִרְאֶ֛ה הֲיִקְרְךָ֥ דְבָרִ֖י אִם לֹֽא

verses.restored: Moses went out and spoke words of YHWH to people; he gathered seventy men from elders of people and made them stand around tent.

familiar.text: And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the LORD, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.

modern.text: So Moses went out and relayed to the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֞ף שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֹתָ֖ם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הָאֹֽהֶל

verses.restored: YHWH came down in cloud and spoke to him; he took from spirit that was upon him and put it upon seventy elders. When spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but did not continue.

familiar.text: And the LORD came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.

modern.text: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied—but they never did so again.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨רֶד יְהוָ֥ה בֶּעָנָן֮ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָיו֒ וַיָּ֗אצֶל מִן הָר֨וּחַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַיִּתֵּ֕ן עַל שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים וַיְהִ֗י כְּנ֤וֹחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָר֔וּחַ וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יָסָֽפוּ

verses.restored: Two men remained in camp; name of one was Eldad and name of second Medad. Spirit rested upon them—they were among those registered but had not gone out to tent—and they prophesied in camp.

familiar.text: But there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.

modern.text: Two men, however, had remained in the camp—one named Eldad and the other Medad—and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׁאֲר֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי אֲנָשִׁ֣ים בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֡ה שֵׁ֣ם הָאֶחָ֣ד אֶלְדָּ֡ד וְשֵׁם֩ הַשֵּׁנִ֨י מֵידָ֜ד וַתָּ֧נַח עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם הָר֗וּחַ וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ בַּכְּתֻבִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָצְא֖וּ הָאֹ֑הֱלָה וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: A young man ran and told Moses, saying, Eldad and Medad are prophesying in camp.

familiar.text: And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.

modern.text: A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”

original.text: וַיָּ֣רָץ הַנַּ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לְמֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֶלְדָּ֣ד וּמֵידָ֔ד מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: Joshua son of Nun, attendant of Moses from his youth, answered and said, My lord Moses, restrain them.

familiar.text: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.

modern.text: Joshua son of Nun, the attendant to Moses since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”

original.text: וַיַּ֜עַן יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן נ֗וּן מְשָׁרֵ֥ת מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִבְּחֻרָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנִ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה כְּלָאֵֽם

verses.restored: Moses said to him, Are you jealous for me? Would that all people of YHWH were prophets, that YHWH would put his spirit upon them!

familiar.text: And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!

modern.text: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַֽמְקַנֵּ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לִ֑י וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן כָּל עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ נְבִיאִ֔ים כִּי יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת רוּח֖וֹ עֲלֵיהֶֽם

familiar.text: And Moses gat him into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

modern.text: Then Moses returned to the camp, along with the elders of Israel. The Quail and the Plague

original.text: וַיֵּאָסֵ֥ף מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה ה֖וּא וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: A wind went out from YHWH and drove quail from sea and let them fall beside camp, about a day's journey this side and a day's journey that side, around camp, and about two cubits above face of ground.

familiar.text: And there went forth a wind from the LORD, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, as it were a day’s journey on this side, and as it were a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and as it were two cubits high upon the face of the earth.

modern.text: Now a wind sent by the LORD came up, drove in quail from the sea, and brought them near the camp, about two cubits above the surface of the ground, for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.

original.text: וְר֜וּחַ נָסַ֣ע מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֣גָז שַׂלְוִים֮ מִן הַיָּם֒ וַיִּטֹּ֨שׁ עַל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה כְּדֶ֧רֶךְ י֣וֹם כֹּ֗ה וּכְדֶ֤רֶךְ יוֹם֙ כֹּ֔ה סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּכְאַמָּתַ֖יִם עַל פְּנֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: The people rose all that day and all night and all next day and gathered quail; one gathering least gathered ten homers, and they spread them all around camp.

familiar.text: And the people stood up all that day, and all that night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quails: he that gathered least gathered ten homers: and they spread them all abroad for themselves round about the camp.

modern.text: All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.

verses.restored: While flesh was still between their teeth, before it was cut, anger of YHWH burned against people, and YHWH struck people with very great plague.

familiar.text: And while the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the LORD was kindled against the people, and the LORD smote the people with a very great plague.

modern.text: But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a severe plague.

original.text: הַבָּשָׂ֗ר עוֹדֶ֨נּוּ֙ בֵּ֣ין שִׁנֵּיהֶ֔ם טֶ֖רֶם יִכָּרֵ֑ת וְאַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ חָרָ֣ה בָעָ֔ם וַיַּ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ בָּעָ֔ם מַכָּ֖ה רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד

familiar.text: And he called the name of that place Kibrothhattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.

modern.text: So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.

familiar.text: And the people journeyed from Kibrothhattaavah unto Hazeroth; and abode at Hazeroth.

modern.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.

original.text: מִקִּבְר֧וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֛ה נָסְע֥וּ הָעָ֖ם חֲצֵר֑וֹת וַיִּהְי֖וּ בַּחֲצֵרֽוֹת

translation_notes: Moses' statements in verses 11-15 are leadership-collapse and death-wish language. The text does not shame him; the immediate Divine response is shared leadership.
The seventy elders receive spirit so burden is distributed rather than concentrated in one leader.
Eldad and Medad prophesy outside the expected location, and Moses refuses Joshua's attempt to monopolize spiritual authority.
Verse 25's final phrase is textually debated and may mean they did not continue or did not cease; it requires witness audit.
The people's craving must not be reduced to mockery of appetite or cultural food memory. The narrative critiques rejection of liberation and destructive excess.
The plague is ancient judgment narrative and must not be used to blame people for illness, hunger, addiction, or eating behavior.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 11 to shame overwhelmed leaders, people in mental-health crisis, hungry communities, migrants remembering familiar food, or those suffering illness. The chapter's clearest constructive movement is from impossible solitary burden to shared spirit and distributed leadership.
